text:
sam: Heads-up — observed weird page stickiness on long-run Qwen-MQA inference. Evicted pages are often reallocated immediately to the same logical slots, increasing fragmentation over time.
lia: repro steps?
sam: Run the nightly stability job with seq=4096, rope_scale=0.5, batch=8 on qwen-2.2-mqa. After ~30m we see oscillating free counts and growing jump in resident set.
tom: can you paste the small perf snippet?
sam: here are the hot lines from the tracer snapshot:
```
kv_page_allocs=67214 kv_page_frees=67150 sticky_rebinds=1248
free_list_len=48 slabs_in_use=372 slack_pages=3
model=qwen-2.2-mqa seq=4096 rope_scale=0.5 kernel=matmul_f32->matmul_f16 switch_count=19
```
lia: interesting the kernel switch count lines up with the sticky_rebinds. might be kernel selection thrash causing allocator to prefer different page sizes?
jess: did you try forcing single kernel path to see if allocator stabilizes?
sam: yes — pinned matmul_f16 at runtime; sticky_rebinds drop to ~20 and fragmentation growth flattens. suggests interplay between kernel selection decisions + page size rounding.
tom: any model specificity? does llama/mistral show same?
sam: quick matrix:
- llama-2-13b-gqa: minor, happens only at seq>8192 and with rope_scale>1.0.
- mistral-8x: almost none, but we see ghost pages when using MQA variant with very short prefixes.
- qwen-2.2-mqa: worst, consistent stickiness at ~30–90 minutes.
lia: hypothesis: MQA layout + rope scaling changes KV slot footprint per layer, kernel switch changes alignment, allocator rounds to page sizes -> causes rebind to different slab class, then immediate reuse looks like eviction+realloc rather than reuse.
jess: that would also explain the per-layer periodicity you saw, sam. any telemetry that correlates layer index to alloc churn?
sam: yes — profiler heatmap shows peaks every ~64 tokens which maps to layer groups where we switch kernel path. pasted short output:
```
layer_alloc_spike: [12, 13, 76, 77, 140, 141] token_offsets ~ [64,128,192]
alloc_latency_ms 1.2 -> 9.8 during spikes
```
lia: is the batching heuristic exacerbating it? larger batches increase chance of a kernel pick that mismatches the previous request's layout.
tom: could try two mitigations: 1) prefer stable kernel choice per model/seq distribution for first N tokens, 2) make allocator coalesce small slabs and avoid rebinds within X ms.
jess: +1 on allocator cooldown. also add a metric for "rebind_rate" so we can alert if > threshold.
infra-bot: deploy queued: kv-alloc-cooldown v0.1 -> staging (CI passes).
sam: I'll run a 6h stability with cooldown=200ms and kernel-pin warmup=128 tokens. will post results.
lia: thanks — if repro clears, we should bake this into Dedicated profiles as a quantization/rope compatibility note.
sam: noted. cc @product-ops for rollout docs. :eyes:
